name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,183

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Voice-activated app inputting question and answer about Middle Eastern people

indicators.note: to input is to feed something inside, so the app's name takes the other letters within it
about here means turned round, so the whole combination is read from the far end

blocks.note: Siri is Apple's voice assistant
Q is the standard abbreviation for question
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A smartphone assistant is asked questions about people from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: Q and A go into the middle of SIRI to make SIQARI, and that whole string read backwards gives IRAQIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraqis are citizens of Iraq, a country in the Middle East, so they are a Middle Eastern people.

clue.text: Short attack on unfinished poem presented logically

indicators.note: something short lacks its end, so the final letter is cut off
unfinished work stops before the end, so the poem word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a raid is an attack
a sonnet is a fourteen-line poem

explanation.surface: A brief verbal attack on an incomplete poem is set out logically.
explanation.walkthrough: RAID loses its D and SONNET loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Raisonné, a French borrowing, means systematically arranged or reasoned, as in a catalogue raisonné.

clue.text: Defiant gesture, not quite defeated over length of dash

indicators.note: not quite all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped
over here means covering, so the shortened word lies across the dash term

blocks.note: quelled means put down or defeated
an en dash is a printer's dash one en long

explanation.surface: A rebellious gesture, almost crushed, lasts only the length of a sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' suggests a sprint, but an en is a printer's measure and an en dash is a dash of that width.
explanation.definitionFit: The quenelle is a provocative arm gesture popularised by the French comedian Dieudonné, read as defiance of the establishment.

clue.text: Runaway rescuable in Calais, an indication of exasperation

definitions.text: in Calais, an indication of exasperation

indicators.note: a runaway has broken loose, so these letters escape their order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A runaway who can still be rescued turns up in Calais, to someone's annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: Calais is the French Channel port, signalling that the exclamation is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacré bleu is the stock French oath of dismay or irritation, so what a Frenchman says when exasperated.

clue.text: Brilliant creature in past beset by routine trouble

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded, so the word for past sits inside the word for routine

blocks.note: a rut is a dull fixed routine
as in walking by, meaning past
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A glittering animal from the past suffers from the trouble of routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brilliant' reads as clever, but it means glittering: the creature is a jewel-coloured insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruby-tail is a cuckoo wasp with gleaming metallic red and green colouring, hence a brilliant insect.

clue.text: Letter doctor enclosed, recording name of computer, about part of brain

blocks.note: rho is a Greek letter
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
enc is the abbreviation for enclosed, as at the foot of a letter
an EP is an extended-play record
HAL is the computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A letter from a doctor, with a recording enclosed, names a computer and discusses part of the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhombencephalon is the hindbrain, comprising the cerebellum, pons and medulla oblongata.

clue.text: The lad surrounded by surly youth and Ecstasy drug source

indicators.note: to be surrounded is to be enclosed, so the word for the lad goes inside

blocks.note: a yob is a loutish young man
him refers to the lad
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A boy is hemmed in by a sullen teenager peddling ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: A yob is British slang for a rowdy, aggressive youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Yohimbe is a West African tree whose bark yields the stimulant yohimbine, so it is a source of a drug.

clue.text: Perhaps Watergate aim's mostly concerned with repressing

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the following phrase's word is dropped
to repress is to hold down inside, so the shortened word keeps the aim word within it

blocks.note: about means concerning
the idea is the aim or intention

explanation.surface: It reads like a comment that the Watergate scandal was mostly about cover-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Watergate tempts as the Nixon scandal; split, it is simply a gate for water, and 'Perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An aboideau is a Canadian dyke with a sluice gate holding back tidewater, so a water gate is one example.

clue.text: Learner accepted by good varsity, taking one Italian course

blocks.note: L is the learner driver's plate
in means accepted, as in fashion
G is the abbreviation for good
U for university, which varsity informally means
takings are money coming in
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A student gets a place at a good university and signs up for an Italian course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian course' looks like a language class; it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguini is a flat ribbon pasta, served as a course in an Italian meal.

clue.text: Wind melted icicle encasing black ring

indicators.note: melted ice loses its form, so the letters of the frozen word are reshaped
to encase is to enclose, so the reshaped letters wrap round the other two pieces

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A thawing icicle is described as wrapping round a dark ring.
explanation.walkthrough: ICICLE is rearranged as LIECCI, with B and O slotted in at two places to make LIBECCIO.
explanation.definitionFit: The libeccio is a south-westerly wind that blows across Corsica and the Italian coast.

clue.text: I see Greek sanctuaries rejected a Midwesterner

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so this word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the exclamation of sudden understanding
naoi is the plural of naos, the inner sanctuary of a Greek temple

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledges that Greek temple sanctuaries have been turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ohioan is a native of Ohio, one of the states of the American Midwest.

clue.text: Gently blows over cutting at back for plant that's fragrant to Bard

indicators.note: cutting here means cutting out, so the two letters named are removed from the phrase
back here means sent backwards, so the remaining letters are read from the end

blocks.note: to breathe on something is to blow gently over it
taken as written, the letters to be cut out

explanation.surface: Someone blows softly over a cutting of a plant that Shakespeare thought sweet-smelling.
explanation.walkthrough: BREATHES ON loses AT to give BREHESON, which is reversed. The Bard is Shakespeare, who uses nose-herb in All's Well That Ends Well.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's nose-herb is a sweet-smelling plant, one valued for its scent rather than its taste.

clue.text: Tinder has you on phone, after a passionate love

indicators.note: on the phone only the sound is heard, so this word is taken for its pronunciation

blocks.note: taken as written
mad about something means passionate about it
love is zero in tennis, written O
the letter U sounds like this word

explanation.surface: A dating app's message has a lover on the phone after a passionate encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts U at the end of A, MAD and O. Tinder looks like the dating app, but here it is kindling.
explanation.definitionFit: Amadou is a spongy material made from bracket fungus, formerly used as tinder for lighting fires.

clue.text: Rest with extended weekend's beginning in Malawi city

indicators.note: with here means holding inside, so the rest word carries the other letters within it
a beginning is a first part, so only the opening letter of that word is used

blocks.note: to lie down is to rest
long means extended
the first letter of weekend

explanation.surface: Someone rests at the start of a long weekend in a Malawian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilongwe is the capital city of Malawi, in southern Africa.

clue.text: Playing lightly although covering very loud tracks

indicators.note: to cover is to go over and around, so the although word encloses the music term

blocks.note: while means although
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of tracks

explanation.surface: A musician plays softly despite playing over very loud backing tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing lightly' sounds musical, matching 'very loud', but it means toying or trifling.
explanation.definitionFit: Whifflery means trifling or frivolous behaviour, a lightweight toying with things.

clue.text: Middle note in part becomes euphonious

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is taken, the answer being a stretch inside them

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of becomes and the start of euphonious

explanation.surface: A note in the middle part of a piece of music turns out to sound pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greek music the mese was the central note or string of the scale system.

clue.text: Gentleman entering large town marks stands of nutmegs

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the gentleman word sits within the town word
in a down clue standing up means reading upwards, so the letters run bottom to top

blocks.note: a city is a large town
sir is the form of address to a gentleman
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A gentleman entering a big town notices stalls of nutmegs.
explanation.walkthrough: The marks are the old German currency, and 'stands' is a verb here, saying the whole string is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Myristic comes from Myristica, the botanical genus of the nutmeg tree, so it means relating to nutmegs.

clue.text: Physicist "rationalised" Noah's ark, making Newton see

indicators.note: turning one thing into another, here the abbreviation for Newton is swapped for the one for see
rationalised means reorganised, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force
v, from Latin vide, means see

explanation.surface: A physicist offers a rational account of Noah's ark that Isaac Newton would have to accept.
explanation.walkthrough: In NOAHS ARK the N becomes V, and the result is rearranged. Newton tempts as Isaac; here it is the unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrei Sakharov was the Soviet nuclear physicist behind the hydrogen bomb, later a dissident and Nobel peace laureate.

clue.text: Spiritual Muslim's uncertainty with American from the other side

indicators.note: starting from the other side means reading from the end instead of the start

blocks.note: an if is a doubt or uncertainty
US for American

explanation.surface: A devout Muslim feels doubt alongside an American on the opposite side.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'Spiritual Muslim's' is read as 'Spiritual Muslim is', the 's linking it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sufi follows the mystical, inward-looking tradition of Islam, so is a spiritual Muslim.

clue.text: Having a knees-up dance to reggae or something similar, with new man

blocks.note: ska is a Jamaican music style, forerunner of reggae
N is the abbreviation for new
a king is a man, or piece, in chess

explanation.surface: People have a lively party dancing to reggae music with a new man.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is British slang for a lively party with dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Skanking is the knee-lifting dance done to ska and reggae, so it is dancing in a lifted-knee style.

clue.text: One typically opposing leaf on erect strong-smelling plant

indicators.note: erect means standing upright, so in a down clue the plant word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: a frond is a fern or palm leaf
rue is a pungent herb

explanation.surface: A gardener lays a leaf on a pungent upright plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A frondeur is a rebel or malcontent, after the Fronde revolt in 17th-century France, so someone habitually against authority.

clue.text: Australian fish died with rage over being caught by chance

indicators.note: turned over, so the word for rage is read backwards
something caught is held inside, so the preceding letters go within the word for chance

blocks.note: luck is chance
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: A fish expires furiously after being caught by an angler's chance.
explanation.definitionFit: The luderick is a dark-banded marine fish of eastern Australian coasts, also called blackfish.

clue.text: With heart sinking, summarily execute first person caught opening for service in the evening

definitions.text: opening for service in the evening

indicators.note: the central letter drops down to the bottom, so the word's order is changed

blocks.note: to lynch is to kill without trial
I is the first person pronoun
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Grim scene: a mob lynches someone, the first person caught, as an evening service begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter N of LYNCH moves to the end, which in a down entry means sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The lychnic is the first part of vespers, the lamp-lighting office that begins evening prayer in the Eastern Church.

clue.text: Island area circled westward by German eight, where long boat trip ended

indicators.note: to be circled is to be surrounded, so the word for area sits inside
in an across clue westward is right to left, so the German word runs backwards

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for island
acht is German for eight
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A region of an island is crossed by a German rowing eight heading west, ending a long voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: ACHT reversed is THCA, and A goes into its middle. The long boat trip is Odysseus's ten-year voyage home in the Odyssey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ithaca was Odysseus's home island, where his wanderings in Homer's Odyssey finally finished.

clue.text: Husband temporarily disliking sister and grand musical humorist

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
to be off something is to have gone off it for now
a nun is a religious sister
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A husband briefly goes off his sister and a great comic musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerard Hoffnung was a German-born British cartoonist and tuba player famous for comic music festivals.

clue.text: This old reindeer with feathers could supply a humiliating punishment

definitions.text: with feathers could supply a humiliating punishment

blocks.note: first meaning: an old word for a reindeer or elk-like beast of legend

blocks.clueFragment: with feathers could supply a humiliating punishment
blocks.note: second meaning: split in two, it is the opening of the phrase for coating someone in pitch and plumage

explanation.surface: An old reindeer, decked with feathers, could be the means of disgracing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as TAR AND, add 'feathers' and you have tar and feathers, the mob punishment of coating a victim in tar then plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarand is an archaic name for a reindeer, or a fabled northern beast able to change colour.

clue.text: Sea changes with wind allow having energy in mid-month

indicators.note: having here means holding, so the word for allow keeps the energy letter inside it

blocks.note: to let is to allow
E is the symbol for energy
the ides was the middle day of the Roman month

explanation.surface: Changes at sea brought by the wind allow energetic activity in the middle of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Roman calendar the ides fell on the 13th or 15th day, the middle of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee tides are tidal currents running in the same direction the wind blows, the tide moving with the wind.

clue.text: About half a dozen cereal seeds for ruminant, say

blocks.note: ca is short for circa, about
VI is six in Roman numerals
corn is the grain of cereal crops

explanation.surface: Roughly six grains of cereal are fed to a cow or other cud-chewer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavicorn is a hollow-horned ruminant, such as cattle, sheep or antelope; 'say' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Huntsmen, yours out of season?

indicators.note: out of here means outside, so the abbreviation wraps round the other word

blocks.note: yrs is the letter-writer's abbreviation for yours
to season timber or cheese is to age it

explanation.surface: Hunters wonder whether something of yours is out of the hunting season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of season' looks like a hunting phrase, but 'out of' means outside and 'season' is the verb to mature.
explanation.definitionFit: Yager is an anglicised form of German Jäger, a hunter, later a rifleman in light infantry.
